title: Friction and Play in a Joint: Stick and Slip, a Gear With a Gap in It, and Which Encoder the Loop Should Watch

questions.question: Why does a joint stick and then slip at low speed?
options: Friction is higher at rest than when sliding (the Stribeck part), so it has to break free
questions.explanation: More to start than to keep going.

questions.question: The friction torque peaked at 0.017 rad/s at 0.0559 N m, and then:
options: Fell to 0.0503 N m at 0.05 rad/s, and grew again with the speed

questions.question: Following a slow ramp, the error without and with the friction fed forward was:
questions.explanation: The feedforward does the work the integral did late.

questions.question: The play of 0.0100 rad was measured as:
questions.explanation: The motor's travel before the load moves.

questions.question: What does closing the position loop, with an integral, on the load's encoder do with play in the gear?
options: Puts the dead zone inside the loop: it hunts (0.0013 rad over a second)

questions.question: What does closing it on the motor's encoder cost?
options: The load is somewhere in the gap: 0.0034 rad off the target
questions.explanation: It controls the motor, not the load.
